In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah Az-Zumar

It is also said: Surah Al-Ghuraf. It is Meccan, except for the verse where He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾, and except for the verse where He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾. It is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: Whoever wishes to know Allah's judgment among His creation, let him recite Surah Al-Ghuraf.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, to the end of the verse. Its meaning: this is the revelation of the Book. It is also said: "The revelation of the Book" is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is "from Allah." His saying: ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾, meaning: the Mighty in His dominion, the Wise in His command.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾. That is, with that which its sending down is due to be, since I have decreed this in the books of the earlier nations. It is also said: "in truth" means by My right over you and over all My creation.

As for His words ﴿So worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾: ikhlas (sincerity) is tawhid (affirming the Oneness of Allah). It is also said: ikhlas is the purifying of intention in obedience to Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿Surely, to Allah belongs the pure religion﴾. That is: the religion in which there is no shirk belongs to Allah, meaning it occurs with His pleasure. As for a religion in which there is shirk, it does not belong to Allah. He mentioned this because there may exist a religion without tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and without sincerity (ikhlas) from it. It is also said: ﴿Surely, to Allah belongs the pure religion﴾, meaning: He ought to be made one, and none is to be associated with Him, and this is not appropriate for anyone else. And from Qatadah, he said: "Surely, to Allah belongs the pure religion": it is the saying of the speaker, "There is no god but Allah."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him [say]: "We only worship them"﴾. That is: protectors besides Allah. ﴿[Ma] nAbudahum (We only worship them)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, [Ibn] Mas'ud and Mujahid recited: "Ma na'budahum (We only worship them)." In the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Ma na'budukum (We only worship you)." The meaning according to the well-known reading: that is, they said, "We only worship them," or they say, "We only worship them," meaning: we only worship the angels ﴿except that they may bring us near to Allah in nearness﴾. That is: closeness.

The meaning of the verse: they intercede for us with Allah.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ﴾. He means: on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and ungrateful﴾. That is: a liar against Allah, ungrateful for the blessings of Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 4–5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If God had wished to take a son, He would have chosen whatever He willed from what He creates﴾, meaning: He would have chosen. Then He declared Himself free of such things, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, meaning: it is not fitting for Him to do so, and it does not befit His purity.

And His saying: ﴿He is God, the One, the Subduer﴾, meaning: One in His essence, and the Subduer over His servants.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 4–5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If God had wished to take a son, He would have chosen whatever He willed from what He creates﴾, meaning: He would have chosen. Then He declared Himself free of such things, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, meaning: it is not fitting for Him to do so, and it does not befit His purity.

And His saying: ﴿He is God, the One, the Subduer﴾, meaning: One in His essence, and the Subduer over His servants.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 6:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He created you from a single soul﴾, that is, Adam. And His saying: ﴿and from it He created its mate﴾, that is, Hawwa' (Eve). We have already explained that He created her from one of his ribs.

And His saying: ﴿And He sent down for you eight pairs of cattle﴾, that is, He created for you eight pairs of cattle. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts﴾, meaning, We created it, and like His saying: ﴿And We sent down iron, in which is great might﴾, meaning, We created it. In some tafsirs it is stated that Allah, the Exalted, created the cattle in the lowest heaven [then] sent them down to the earth. They are eight pairs: a male camel and a female camel, a bull and a cow, a ram and a ewe, and a he-goat and a she-goat.

In the Tafsir of al-Naqqash: Allah, the Exalted, sent down to Adam the mi'lah (tongs/anvil-holder), the hammer, and the two pincers. He was on a mountain, and he saw a firm iron rod, so he took it and struck the trees with it, and they were dry, so the trees broke, meaning the trees. Then he struck fire from the iron and the stone, and he kindled the trees under the iron until it melted. Then he shaped from it a knife (madya). After that he made from it an oven (tannur), which is the baking oven, and that was the first thing Adam made from it.

And His saying: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾, that is, drops of semen, then clots, then lumps of flesh, then bones.

And His saying: ﴿in three darknesses﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta. And from some of them: the darkness of the loins, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the belly, and this is because the child is created when it is created in the womb, then it rises to the belly.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion; there is no god but He; so how are you turned away?﴾, that is, away from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions. The first: He does not approve for His believing servants disbelief.

The second: that He does not approve for all of His servants disbelief. According to this opinion, a distinction is made between the will (irada) and the approval (rida), and he said: sins are by the will of Allah, exalted is He, but not by His approval and love. This has been transmitted from Qatadah. Both opinions are possible.

The second is the more preferable and closer to the school of the early generations (al-salaf).

His saying: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾, meaning: He chooses gratitude for you. His saying: ﴿And no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾, meaning: no one is made to bear a sin committed by someone else. His saying: ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 8:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾. That is: affliction and hardship. ﴿He calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾: returning to Him.

And His words: ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favour from Himself﴾. That is: He gives him. The poet said: (He gives and does not withhold, and does not hold back, the summit-heaped camel-mounts of the one who bestows [khawal]).

And His words: ﴿a favour from Himself﴾: a gift from Him. And His words: ﴿he forgets what he used to call upon Him for before﴾: that is, he forgets the supplication he used to make before. It is also said: he forgets God, whom he used to call upon before.

And His words: ﴿and sets up rivals to God, to lead others astray from His way﴾: that is, he ascribes to God rivals and likenesses. And His words: ﴿to lead others astray from His way﴾: that is, from the way of truth.

And His words: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire"﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection. The people of tafsir said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Hudhayfah ibn al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah al-Makhzumi. It is said: it refers to every disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 9:

His saying, Most High: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾. It was read: "Amman huwa qanit". That is, obedient (muti'), and it was said: standing (qa'im). His saying: ﴿during the hours of the night﴾, that is, the periods of the night. His saying: ﴿prostrating and standing﴾, that is, prostrating upon his face and standing upon his feet, like one whose state is not this, and this is what we mentioned before. It was also said: "Is this one better, or that one?" As for the reading with the lightened form (taskhif), there are two opinions concerning it. The first: "Amman huwa qanit" meaning "Is one who is devoutly obedient like one who is not devoutly obedient?" The other opinion: its meaning is "O you who are devoutly obedient," as a vocative address. The poet said: (O sons of Lubayna, you are not a hand ... except a hand that has no arm)

That is, "O sons of Lubayna." The opinions differed concerning who the verse was revealed about. From Ibn 'Umar it is related that it was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan. From al-Dahhak it is related that it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them. Al-Kalbi related that it was revealed concerning Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ammar and Salman. In some narrations: Abu Dharr and Suhayb were with them.

His saying: ﴿fearing the Hereafter﴾, that is, fearing the Hereafter, (and hoping for the mercy of his Lord), that is, longing for the mercy of his Lord.

His saying: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ meaning: they are not equal. It is said: those who know are the believers, and those who do not know are the disbelievers. It is also said: those who know are the scholars, and those who do not know are the ignorant.

Al-Naqqash related in his tafsir from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir that he said: those who know are our lovers and our partisans (shi'ah), and those who do not know are our enemies. His saying: ﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾, that is, those of intellect (uli al-'uqul).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 10:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord.﴾ That is: be wary of your Lord and fear Him.

And His saying: ﴿For those who do good in this world there is good.﴾ "Do good" means: believe. It is also said: do good through obedience to God. And His saying: ﴿in this world there is good﴾ means: health and well-being. It is also said: abundant provision. And it is said: a life lived in obedience to God.

And His saying: ﴿And God's earth is spacious.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: whoever is commanded to commit sins, let him flee. The verse contains a command to emigrate from a land in which sins are openly committed to a land in which sins are not openly committed. It is also said regarding it: "God's earth is spacious" means Madinah, so he commanded migration from Makkah to Madinah. It is also said: the verse was revealed concerning Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and his companions, when they emigrated from Makkah to Abyssinia.

And His saying: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward﴾ that is: estrangement and leaving one's homeland, fleeing with their religion. ﴿Their reward without reckoning﴾ means: without measure.

It is reported in a report that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾, I said: 'My Lord, increase my ummah.' Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears﴾. Then he said: 'Increase my ummah.' So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without reckoning.﴾"

And it is reported from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: Every obedient person is measured out by measure and weighed by weight, except the patient; for they are given without measure, poured out in handfuls.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Indeed I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ That is, sincere to Him in monotheism (tawhid). The sincerity of tawhid is that you do not associate anything else with Him.
And His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾, meaning: the first of the Muslims from Quraysh. His saying

Most High said: ﴿Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ Meaning: if I disobey my Lord by associating partners with Him (shirk). It is also said: by associating partners with Him and by other than that. It is permissible that the address is directed to him (the Prophet ﷺ), while what is intended is his community (ummah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "It is God I worship, devoted to Him in my religion."﴾ That is: my monotheism (tawhid).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 15:

And His saying: ﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾ is in the manner of a threat and a warning.

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection."﴾ If someone says: what is the meaning of the loss of the families (al-ahlin)?

We say: the answer has two aspects. The first: there is no one except that he has a people (ahl) in Paradise by his name. So when he disbelieves and enters the Fire, he has lost his people, in the sense that the one who was by his name is given to another.

The second aspect: the loss of the self is by his being made to enter the Fire, and the loss of the family is by his being separated from his family.

And His saying: ﴿Is not that the clear loss?﴾ means: the clear (al-bayn) one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For them there will be canopies of fire above them, and canopies below them.﴾ The word "ẓulal" (canopies) is the plural of "ẓullah" (canopy), and the ẓullah is a mountain. What is meant by His saying "ẓulal" is the abundance of the punishment. As for His saying ﴿and below them canopies﴾, we have already explained it.

His saying: ﴿With this, God frightens His servants.﴾ That is, He warns them.

His saying: ﴿So fear Me, O My servants.﴾ That is, beware of My punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verses 17–18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it﴾, meaning: the Shaytan (devil). It is said: al-Taghut (the transgressing idol/false deity) is a non-Arabic word. It is also said: it is an Arabic word derived from al-tughyan (transgression).

And His saying: ﴿and turn back to Allah﴾, meaning: they returned to Allah.

And His saying: ﴿for them is good tidings﴾, meaning: the glad tidings of Paradise. And His saying: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾.

Regarding the verse there are several opinions:

The first: "they listen to the word," meaning the Qur'an, "and follow the best of it." The best of it is pardoning, and retaliation against the wrongdoer is mentioned in the Qur'an, and pardoning is also mentioned; pardoning is the better of the two.

The second opinion: "they listen to the word," meaning they listen to the Qur'an and other than the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾, meaning the Qur'an. Some of them said: they listen to the concessions (rukhas) and the firm obligations ('aza'im), and they follow the best of them, meaning the firm obligations.

The fourth opinion: "they listen to the word," meaning the speech, "and follow the best of it," meaning the statement "There is no god but Allah."

And His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾, meaning: Allah has guided them to the truth.

And His saying: ﴿And those are the people of understanding﴾, meaning: the people of intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verses 17–18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it﴾, meaning: the Shaytan (devil). It is said: al-Taghut (the transgressing idol/false deity) is a non-Arabic word. It is also said: it is an Arabic word derived from al-tughyan (transgression).

And His saying: ﴿and turn back to Allah﴾, meaning: they returned to Allah.

And His saying: ﴿for them is good tidings﴾, meaning: the glad tidings of Paradise. And His saying: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾.

Regarding the verse there are several opinions:

The first: "they listen to the word," meaning the Qur'an, "and follow the best of it." The best of it is pardoning, and retaliation against the wrongdoer is mentioned in the Qur'an, and pardoning is also mentioned; pardoning is the better of the two.

The second opinion: "they listen to the word," meaning they listen to the Qur'an and other than the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾, meaning the Qur'an. Some of them said: they listen to the concessions (rukhas) and the firm obligations ('aza'im), and they follow the best of them, meaning the firm obligations.

The fourth opinion: "they listen to the word," meaning the speech, "and follow the best of it," meaning the statement "There is no god but Allah."

And His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾, meaning: Allah has guided them to the truth.

And His saying: ﴿And those are the people of understanding﴾, meaning: the people of intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 19:

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has come due...﴾ "The word of punishment" is His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together﴾. And it is said: "The word of punishment" is His statement: "These are in the Fire and I do not mind."

And His statement: ﴿Would you then save those who are in the Fire?﴾ That is: you cannot rescue him.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have lofty chambers, one above another, built on high, beneath which rivers flow. It is the promise of Allah; Allah does not fail in His promise.﴾ That is, His promise.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 39, verse 21:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth?﴾ That is: He causes it to run as rivers in the earth.

And His saying: ﴿Then He brings out by it crops of varying colors﴾ That is: yellow, red, and green.

And His saying: ﴿Then it dries up﴾ That is: it withers. It is said: "hāja al-nabāt" (the plant dried up) when it dries.

And His saying: ﴿Then you see it turn yellow﴾ That is: you see the plant turning yellow. And His saying: ﴿Then He makes it debris (ḥuṭām)﴾ That is: crumbled pieces (fatāt). And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ The meaning is clear, and "dhikrā" (reminder) means "tadhkira" (a reminding).

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 39, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord…﴾ means: Allah has widened his breast for Islam.

And His saying: ﴿so he is upon a light from his Lord﴾. In the report: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When light enters the heart of the believer, it expands and becomes spacious." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a sign of that?" He said: "Yes: withdrawing from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before death arrives."

And His saying: ﴿so he is upon a light from his Lord﴾ may refer to the light being before he embraces Islam, and it may refer to it being after Islam, as a fruit of his Islam. As for the expansion of the breast, it is the preparation for Islam and its groundwork.

And His saying: ﴿So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾ means: those who do not remember Allah. Everyone who abandons the remembrance of Allah has had his heart hardened. His saying: ﴿those are in manifest error﴾ means: clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. He called it "statement" (hadith) because it is a statement of His sending down. It was also said: "Allah has sent down the best statement" means: the best speech.

It has been transmitted in the reports: "The superiority of the speech of Allah over the speech of His creation is like His superiority over His creation."

His saying: ﴿a Book, its parts resembling one another﴾, meaning: some of it resembles other parts in truthfulness and soundness of meaning. It is also said: "mutashabihan" means: verse after verse, and surah after surah.

His saying: ﴿oft-repeated﴾ (mathani), meaning: in it are repeated the mention of promise and threat, and the mention of command and prohibition. It is also said: "mathani" means: verse after verse, and surah after surah.

His saying: ﴿the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it﴾, meaning: the hearts of those who fear their Lord. He used "skins" as a metonymy for "hearts." It is also said: the meaning of "skins" is the skins themselves. In some reports: "Whoever is seized by a shiver from the fear of Allah, the Exalted, his sins fall away from him as the leaves of a tree fall away."

His saying: ﴿then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning: by the remembrance of Allah. The real meaning is that their hearts shiver at fear and soften at hope.

His saying: ﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He wills﴾, meaning: whom He wills of His servants. And His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, meaning: no one who gives direction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 24:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one who shields with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [as one who is safe]?﴾ On this there are two opinions. The first is that he is dragged in the Fire, dragged upon his face.

The second opinion: ﴿Is one who shields with his face from the evil of the punishment﴾ because the hand of the disbelievers will be shackled, so he shields the punishment with his face, just as a man shields himself with his hand.

As for His saying: ﴿And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn."﴾, its meaning is apparent.
And His saying, ﴿Those before them denied﴾, means: they denied the Resurrection. And His saying, ﴿So the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾, means: they did not know.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So Allah made them taste disgrace in the life of this world﴾, meaning: the punishment that humiliates them. And His saying: ﴿But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾, meaning: the punishment of the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire, is greater than every punishment.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾. That is, similitude (mathal) and likeness. And His words: ﴿so that they may take heed﴾ mean: that they may take heed of the parables (amthal) contained in it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness﴾, meaning: We sent down an Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, that is, without any ambiguity (labs). Mujahid said: It is also said: without any contradiction (ikhtilaf), because part of it confirms the other part. Al-Walibi related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "without any crookedness" means: uncreated (ghayr makhluq). Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna related from seventy of the Successors (tabi'un) that the Qur'an is neither creator nor created. This wording is also transmitted from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin. And His saying: ﴿so that they may be mindful of God﴾, meaning: that they may fear God (yattaqun Allah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 39, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah sets forth an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man﴾. He means: "mutashakisun" (mutually contentious, difficult to satisfy one another). And His saying: ﴿and a man belonging wholly to one man﴾ means: a pure devotion to one man. This is a parable for the believer and the disbeliever: the disbeliever worships many idols, while the believer worships none but Allah alone.

And His saying: ﴿Are the two alike in description?﴾ means: are they similar? And His saying: ﴿All praise is for Allah; but most of them do not know﴾ means: praise is due to Me for what I have made clear of the truth. And His saying: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ means: the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾, meaning: you will die. Al-mayyit (ميت) and al-mayt (ميْت) are one and the same, though some scholars distinguished between them. They said: al-mayyit is the one who has actually died, while al-mayt is the one who is going to die. The poet said:

(He who has died and found rest is not a mayyit... rather, the true mayyit is the mayyit of the living)

The benefit of the verse is that God, exalted is He, made clear that Muhammad (ﷺ) would die, because He knew that his companions differed about his death.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 31:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute with one another﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

In some of the musnads, with a narration from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam (رضي الله عنه), that when this verse was revealed, he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, will the matters of the major sins that were between us be repeated to us?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes." Al-Zubayr said: "Indeed, the matter is then severe."

And from Abdullah ibn Umar (رضي الله عنه), who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute with one another﴾, we did not know what this dispute was, until what happened among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) occurred; so we understood that this is it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 32:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Their lying about Allah consists in the Jews claiming that 'Uzayr is the son of Allah, and the Christians claiming that the Messiah is the son of Allah.

Some of them said: Their lying about Allah is denying the prophets of Allah. As-Suddi said: It is shirk (associating partners with Allah). The Quraysh also claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah.

His words: ﴿and denies the truth when it has come to him﴾, meaning: the Qur'an when it has come to him. It is also said: the Messenger when he has come to him. His words: ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ are an interrogative used in the sense of affirmation (taqrir, establishing a fact by question).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 33:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And he who brings the truth and confirms it﴾. The most apparent of the opinions is that the meaning of His saying ﴿he who brings the truth﴾ is Muhammad (ﷺ), and ﴿confirms it﴾ refers to the believers. In the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, it is: "And those who bring the truth and confirm it." The meaning of His saying ﴿those who bring the truth﴾ is the believers, ﴿and confirm it﴾, that is, they confirmed it in this world, and they brought the truth in the Hereafter. Mujahid interpreted the well-known recitation according to this.

The people of linguistics (ahl al-lughah) said: "alladhina" (those) and "alladhi" (he who) may be used with the same meaning. The poet said:

(And indeed those whose blood was shed at Falaj
they are the people, all of the people, O Umm Khalid)

The second opinion regarding the verse is that he who brings the truth is Jibril (peace be upon him), and the one who confirms it is Muhammad.

The third opinion: "He who brings the truth" is Muhammad, and "confirms it" is Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), as stated by Awf ibn Abdullah and others.

The fourth opinion: "He who brings the truth" is Muhammad, and "confirms it" is Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), as related by Layth from Mujahid. His saying ﴿those are the God-fearing﴾ is clear in meaning.

"Their word, may He exalt: ﴿For them is whatever they wish with their Lord﴾" — meaning: whatever they choose.

This verse indicates that the sleeper's soul has left his body, while we know with certainty that the soul is in his body. Do you not see that he breathes and sees dreams, and that this cannot happen except while the soul is present?

The answer to this: the soul (nafs) has two aspects. The first: the discerning soul (al-nafs al-mumayyizah), by which there is perception of things. The second: the soul by which there is life. And in a report: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As you sleep, so you die; and as you awaken, so you are resurrected."

It is also said: a human being has a nafs and a ruh. At sleep the nafs departs while the ruh remains, and this view is close to the first view.

And from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: the ruh departs at sleep and its radiance remains in the body; thereby one sees dreams. When one is woken from sleep, the ruh returns to his body faster than a blink. And Allah knows best.

And it is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he would say at sleep: "O Allah, You take their souls; if You hold them, then forgive them and have mercy on them, and if You release them, then protect them with that with which You protect Your righteous servants."

"Their word, may He exalt: ﴿For them is whatever they wish with their Lord﴾" — meaning: whatever they choose.

"And His words: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ — that is: lessons (ʿibar) for a people who reflect upon Our signs."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah?﴾ That is: idols that intercede for them. This is in the manner of denunciation and rebuke.

And His saying: ﴿Say: "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ That is: they sought intercession from one who possesses nothing and does not understand,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 44:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs all intercession﴾ mean: no one intercedes except with His permission, so intercession comes from Him, since it can only occur with His permission.

As for His words: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned﴾, its meaning is apparent.

It is also narrated that Jibril, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "To Allah belong the heavens and what is in them, and He created the earth and what is in it, and He created what is between them, of what is known and of what is not known."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink (ishmaza'at)﴾, meaning: they recoil and are constricted. And His saying: ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: the disbelievers.

In the tafsir it is related that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say, "There is no god but Allah," they would all recoil from his saying.

And His saying: ﴿But when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice (yastabshirun)﴾, meaning: they are delighted. It is said that this verse was revealed when Satan cast upon the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ) the mention of the idols with intercession, which is his saying, "Those are the exalted cranes (al-gharaniq al-ula), whose intercession is hoped for," as we have mentioned. This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾, because when they heard that, they rejoiced and were delighted, and they said to the Prophet: "O Muhammad, we only wanted from you this: that you not disparage our gods and that you mention them only with goodness. Otherwise, we know that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 46:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, meaning: Creator of the heavens and the earth, ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, meaning: the secret and the manifest.

And His saying: ﴿You judge between Your servants concerning that in which they used to differ﴾, meaning: concerning the matter of their religion. It is related from some of them that he said: "I accompanied al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym for such-and-such years, and I never heard from him a word except the remembrance of Allah, Exalted is He. When al-Husayn - may Allah be pleased with him - was killed, we said: 'Now he will speak about something.' So he was informed of that. When he heard it, he recited this verse: ﴿Say: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ ... the verse."

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if those who did wrong had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom with it﴾. We have already explained this before. It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Allah, may He be exalted, says on the Day of Resurrection to the disbeliever: "Did you see, if you had all the earth filled with gold, would you have ransomed yourself with it?" He says: "Yes." Allah, may He be exalted, says: "I asked you for something far easier than that while you were in your father's loins: that you should not associate anything with Me; but you refused except to associate with Me."

And His saying: ﴿from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: from the punishment that is hideous and severe on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: ﴿and there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾, meaning: there will become apparent to them from Allah what they had not hoped for, and it was not in their reckoning or their assumption. It is narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir became distressed at the time of death, and when he was asked about that, he said: "I fear that there may appear to me from Allah what I had not reckoned."

And [Allah says]: ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they had earned﴾, meaning: the bad consequences of their deeds became apparent to them. And [Allah says]: ﴿And there will befall them that which they used to mock﴾, meaning: there descended upon them the recompense of what they used to ridicule.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 49:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When harm touches man﴾, meaning: hardship and affliction. His saying: ﴿he calls upon Us﴾, meaning: he asks Us to remove it. His saying: ﴿then when We bestow upon him a favour from Us﴾, meaning: We give him a favour from Us.

His saying: ﴿He says, "I have only been given it because of knowledge."﴾ meaning: I have been given it on account of knowledge, i.e., because of my own knowledge and effort. It is also said: "I have been given it on account of God's knowledge concerning me (may His majesty be exalted) that I am deserving of what He has given me." It is also said: "On account of a nobility from me and an honour for me."

His saying: ﴿Rather, it is a trial﴾, meaning: a test and an affliction. His saying: ﴿but most of the people do not know﴾, meaning: they do not know that what We give of favour is a test and an affliction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 50:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Those before them had already said it﴾ mean: those who came before them said this statement. In the exegesis it is related that what is meant by this is Qarun (Qarun), for he said: "I was only given it on account of knowledge that I have."

And His words: ﴿But what they earned did not avail them﴾ mean: what they had acquired did not avail them anything at all.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the evil consequences of what they had earned struck them. And those who wronged among these [people] — the evil consequences of what they earned will strike them﴾. That is: the disbelievers of this community will be struck by the calamity and punishment that struck the earlier nations.

And His saying: ﴿And they cannot escape [Allah]﴾. That is: they will not be able to outrun Him, nor get away.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 52:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Did they not know that Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it?﴾ "Yabsut" means He widens it, and "yaqdir" means He narrows it.

It is related in some reports: "Allah chooses for His servant. If the choice for him lies in abundance, He widens it for him; and if the choice for him lies in restriction, He restricts it for him" (1).

And His words: ﴿Surely in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ means: who affirm the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾. It is said: the verse "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful" was revealed concerning Wahshi, the freedman of Muti' ibn Adi. It is also said: it was revealed concerning a group of the leaders of the disbelievers who embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, such as Suhayl ibn Amr, Hakim ibn Hizam, Safwan ibn Umayyah, and others.

In the tafsir (it is mentioned) that they said: "Muhammad says: whoever associates partners with Allah, or commits adultery, or kills a soul, has perished; and we have done all of this, so what will our state be?" So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse.

It is also narrated that when Wahshi embraced Islam, the Prophet could not bear to see him; so Wahshi thought that his Islam had not been accepted, and Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse.

Thawban narrated from the Prophet that he said: "Nothing in this verse would please me more than the world and all that is in it."

And from Zayd ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: this verse is the most far-reaching verse in the Qur'an.

And from Ubayd ibn Umayr: that Adam, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, You have given Iblis power over me and over my offspring, and I cannot withstand him except by You."

He said: "O Adam, no child is born to you except that I appoint someone to guard him." He said: "O Lord, increase it for me." He said: "The gate of repentance is open to your offspring; it will not be closed until the Hour comes."

He said: "O Lord, increase it for me." He said: "A good deed is (rewarded) tenfold, and an evil deed (is recompensed) with its like."

He said: "O Lord, increase it for me." He said: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah," to the end of the verse.

Ibn Mas'ud recited: "do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah" (la ta'yasu), and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿do not despair﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah forgives all sins; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, its meaning is apparent. The people of tafsir said: He forgives all sins, if He wills.

It is also narrated that when this verse was revealed, a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what of those who associate partners?" The Prophet was silent, then said: "And what of those who associate partners?" The man said: "Except those who associate partners."

It is also narrated that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud passed by a storyteller who was preaching and making the people harsh, and he said: "O man, do not do that," and he recited this verse: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves," to the end of the verse.

Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated from Asma' bint Yazid that the Prophet recited: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins, and He does not mind," mentioned by Abu Isa in his Jami'.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And turn back in repentance to your Lord﴾, means: return to your Lord. His saying ﴿and submit to Him﴾ means: and devote yourselves sincerely to Him. It is also said: "and surrender to Him." His saying ﴿before the punishment comes upon you, and then you will not be helped﴾ means: you will not be prevented.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 55:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "the best" (al-ahsan) earlier. It is also said: ﴿And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾, meaning: the good that has been sent down to you from your Lord.

And His words: ﴿before the punishment comes upon you suddenly﴾, meaning: unexpectedly, ﴿while you do not perceive﴾, meaning: while you do not know.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lest a soul should say﴾ means: follow the obedience of God out of caution and fear lest a soul should say ﴿"Alas, my grief"﴾, that is: "Alas, my regret!" It is also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿"Alas, my grief"﴾ is: "O grief [O (you) grief], this is your time."

And His saying: ﴿"over what I neglected in regard to God"﴾, that is: I wasted in the sight of God.

Mujahid said: "in the matter of God." Al-Hasan said: "in the obedience of God." It was also said: "in the remembrance of God." Some of them said: "over what I neglected of the side that leads to the pleasure of God, exalted is He." It was also said: "in regard to God" means: in the nearness and proximity of God, related by al-Naqqash and others.

And His saying: ﴿"And indeed I was among the mockers"﴾, that is: among those who ridicule.

Translation:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or [lest] it say, "Had Allah guided me, I would surely have been among the God-fearing"﴾. Its meaning: in the manner we have explained concerning caution (al-hadhar).

Translation:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or [that] it say, when it sees the punishment, "If only I had a return [to the world]"﴾, meaning: a return.

And His saying: ﴿so that I might be among the doers of good﴾, meaning: among those who do good in obedience to Allah.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 39, verse 59:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Yes, indeed, My verses came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant﴾, meaning: you acted with arrogance (takabbur). And His saying: ﴿and you were among the disbelievers﴾, meaning: those who denied My blessings (al-jahidin li-ni'mi).

And His saying: ﴿Yes (bala)﴾ at the beginning, its implication is the expression of their regret (tahassur), their remorse (ta'assuf), and their repentance (nadamat) for what had passed.

On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah with their faces blackened. The meaning of "lied against Allah" is: they claimed that Allah has taken a son or a partner. It is also said that it is general, applying to every lie against Allah.

And His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ is a question used in the sense of affirmation (taqrir).

Allah's words: ﴿And Allah will deliver those who were mindful of Him with their triumph﴾, meaning: by the paths that lead them to success and salvation.

And His words: ﴿No harm will touch them, nor will they grieve﴾ are clear.
Allah's saying: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.﴾ That is, the Preserver (ḥāfiẓ). It is also said: the Manager of affairs according to His will (mashī'ah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 63:

Allah's statement: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾ means: with Him are the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. It is also said: the keys (mafatih) of the treasuries. In some reports transmitted through Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet (ﷺ) said, explaining the meaning of al-maqalid (the keys): "Glory be to Allah, Allah is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah, all praise is due to Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness, and there is no power except with Allah. He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and He has knowledge of everything."

This is the explanation of al-maqalid. And they recited, regarding al-iqlid (the key, singular): (The rooster did not crow with a voice that would wake you... nor did you attempt a locked door with a key.)

Allah's statement: ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, they are the losers﴾ means: they lost the reward, and punishment befell them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 64:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "Do you order me to worship other than God, you ignorant ones?"﴾ It is related that the polytheists said to the Prophet: "Touch some of our gods [with your hand], and we will believe in you." And it is related that they said: "We will worship your God for a year, and you worship our gods for a year." So God, may He be exalted, sent down this verse.

His saying: ﴿you ignorant ones﴾, meaning: those who are ignorant of God, His authority, His power and His greatness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 65:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ It is said: this is an address to the Messenger, but what is meant is someone other than him. It is also possible that it is a form of discipline for the Messenger and a warning to him, so that he holds firmly to what he is upon.

As for His saying: ﴿and you will surely be among the losers﴾, that is, those who have lost everything they hoped for.

Translation:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone, and be among the thankful﴾ is an address to the Messenger.

And His saying: ﴿and be among the thankful﴾ means: among those who are thankful for My blessings.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 67:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾. Its meaning: they did not magnify God with His true magnificence. It is also said: they did not describe God with His true description.

And His saying: ﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾. It has been established through the narration of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that a Jew came to the Prophet and said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will place the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains on one finger, and all creation on one finger." The Prophet laughed, and recited His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾. In another narration: "The Prophet laughed out of wonder and in confirmation of him." The report is in the form found in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

In a narration of Ibn Umar from the Prophet: "God will seize the earth and fold the heavens with His right hand, then say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?" Ibn Umar said: "The Prophet began to move on his pulpit, until we said: it is about to fall." In another narration: "The pulpit began to move like this and like this."

In a narration of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Prophet recited: ﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand﴾. Aisha said: "Where will the people be?" He said: "On the Sirat." It is also narrated that he said: "On the bridge of Hell."

It is said that His handful and His right hand are without description (bila wasf). Sufyan ibn Uyayna said: "Whatever comes in the Qur'an of this kind, its interpretation is its recitation," related by al-Naqqash and others. It is also said: His handful is His power, but the first view is more preferable in light of what we have explained earlier.

His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾. He declared Himself free of what the polytheists attribute to Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 68:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown﴾. It is related from some of the early Muslims (al-salaf) that he said: "Whoever wishes to witness the Day of Resurrection, meaning with his heart, let him recite the last surah of az-Zumar."

As for the Trumpet (al-Sur), we have already explained that it is a horn that will be blown into. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr related it from the Prophet.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri related from the Prophet that he said: "How can I be at ease, when the one who holds the horn has put it to his mouth, bent his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting to be commanded so that he may blow?"

As for His saying: ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾, concerning the words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ there are two opinions:

One of them: they are the martyrs. The other: they are Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil and the Angel of Death.

In the tafsir of al-Kalbi and others: Only these four will remain after the Trumpet is blown. Then Allah, the Exalted, will take the soul of Mika'il, and the Angel of Death will take it; then the soul of Israfil, then the soul of the Angel of Death; and the last of them to die will be Jibril, peace be upon him, and they will fall. Jibril's superiority over them will be like the superiority of a mountain over small hills.

As for His saying: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾, meaning: they will be looking to see what is commanded concerning them. It is established from the Prophet, through the narration of Abu Hurayrah, that a Jew said in the marketplace of Madinah: "No, by Him who chose Musa above mankind." A man from the Ansar raised his hand and struck his face, saying: "You lie." They mentioned that to the Prophet, and the Prophet said: "Allah, the Exalted, will raise up creation, and I will be the first to lift my head, and behold, Musa will be holding onto one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he will be raised before me, or whether he is among those whom Allah, the Exalted, excepted?" Then he said: "Whoever says, 'I am better than Musa,' has lied."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the earth shines with the light of its Lord﴾, meaning: with the light of its Creator and Owner. It is reported from al-Hasan: "with the justice of its Lord." It is also said: God creates a light, and the earth of the Resurrection shines with it.

His saying: ﴿And the Book is placed﴾. What is meant by the Book is the book of deeds. It is reported from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib that he said: "The first to be called to account is Gabriel, peace be upon him, because he was the trustworthy one of God over all His revelation." It is also related that the first to be called to account are the Prophets. And it is established in some narrations that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The first matter on which God, may He be exalted, will judge among the creatures is blood."

His saying: ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses are brought﴾, meaning: those who bear witness for the prophets that they conveyed the message, and against the nations that they denied it. We have already explained this earlier.

His saying: ﴿And it is judged between them with truth﴾, meaning: with justice. His saying: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: no addition will be made to their evil deeds, and nothing will be diminished from their good deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 70:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do﴾. That is: what they make. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Allah, may He be exalted, commands one who calls out on the Day of Resurrection: "O people of Paradise, indeed for you is that you will live and never die, and that you will be healthy and never fall ill, and that you will be young and never grow old, and that you will enjoy bounty and never be miserable." Then he (ﷺ) recited His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 71:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾ — meaning: in companies (afwaj), one group after another (zumrah ba'da zumrah). And His saying: ﴿until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?"﴾ — meaning: they will frighten you (yukhawwifunakum).

And His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers."﴾ — this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with the jinn and mankind all together"﴾ (Q. 32:13), and His saying: ﴿upon the disbelievers﴾. The meaning of "haqqat" (has come due) is "wajabat" (was necessary/obligatory).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ That is: the dwelling-place of those who were arrogant towards faith in Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 73:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾.

Know that according to the Kufans this waw (the "and" in "and its gates are opened") is elided in meaning, whereas according to the Basrans it is not elided. The estimated sense according to the Basran view is: "until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, they enter it."

As for His words: ﴿And its keepers will say to them: Peace be upon you; you have been good﴾, meaning: you have been blessed (ni'mtum, i.e., you have prospered). It is also said: you have been made sound (sahhahtum) for Paradise. It is related from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "At the gate of Paradise there will be two springs. The believer will bathe in one of them, so his outward appearance will be purified, and he will drink from the other, so his inward being will be purified. Then Allah will admit him into Paradise." And he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿You have been good, so enter it, abiding forever﴾.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us"﴾, meaning: He kept His promise to us and completed it. And His saying: ﴿and has made us inherit the land﴾, meaning: the land of Paradise, ﴿to dwell therein wherever we will﴾, meaning: to settle therein wherever we wish. ﴿How excellent is the reward of those who work [righteousness]﴾, meaning: those who perform acts of obedience."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 39, verse 75:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying [their] Lord with praise﴾, meaning: encircling it, surrounding it. His saying: ﴿glorifying with the praise of their Lord﴾, meaning: by the command of their Lord. It is also said: they glorify, praising their Lord. It is said that this glorification is the glorification of delight (tasbih talladhdhudh), not of worship (tasbih ta'abbud).

His saying: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾, meaning: with justice.

His saying: ﴿And it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ meaning: the people of Paradise will say, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." It has been mentioned in another place: ﴿And the last of their call will be, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ We have explained this before.
